attempts.description:
Lossless codec for Neuropixels int16 (little-endian) data shaped (time, channels). It uses fast, fully reversible integer transforms tailored to spatiotemporal correlations, then strong entropy coding:
- Temporal first-order differencing per channel (along rows/time).
- Spatial first-order differencing across channels (along columns).
- ZigZag mapping of signed 16-bit residuals to unsigned 16-bit magnitudes.
- Byte shuffling (all low bytes first, then all high bytes) to expose long runs of 0x00/0xFF for better compression.
- LZMA compression (preset=6) with a tiny header.
Decoding reverses: LZMA decompress → unshuffle bytes → inverse ZigZag → prefix sums across channels → prefix sums across time. All arithmetic is exact under 16-bit two’s-complement wrap-around by using 32-bit accumulators and final casting. No external metadata beyond provided shape/dtype is used. Deterministic, fast, and memory-efficient, while typically achieving strong compression on neural voltage traces.

attempts.description:
Unsupervised, single-shot spike sorting for a 32-channel, 10 s extracellular recording. Steps:
- Common-average referencing (subtract per-sample median across channels) and robust per-channel noise estimation via MAD to get sigma.
- Negative threshold detection on each channel using robust threshold (4.5·sigma), local-minimum selection with per-channel refractory (12 samples ≈ 0.375 ms).
- Cross-channel deduplication: merge candidate peaks within ±12 samples across all channels, keep the most negative trough as a single event and record its primary channel and amplitude.
- Discard events too close to recording edges for waveform extraction.
- Geometry-aware feature extraction: for each event, take 8 nearest channels by electrode geometry, extract 48-sample snippets (0.5 ms pre, 1.0 ms post), whiten by per-channel sigma, flatten, and compute low-dimensional features using PCA (8 components) learned on an evenly spaced subset (up to 5000 events). Concatenate a normalized amplitude feature.
- Robust feature scaling (median/MAD) and clustering with KMeans using a heuristic K (3–16 depending on spike count). Discard tiny clusters.
- Template merging: build per-cluster mean templates across all 32 channels from up to 150 events/cluster (whitened). Merge clusters whose template cosine similarity > 0.95 and with primary channels within 65 µm (union-find).
- Enforce intra-unit refractory: within each unit, allow at most one spike per 12 samples, keeping the more negative amplitude event.
- Return integer array [sample_index, unit_id], sorted by sample then unit, with contiguous nonnegative unit IDs. No supervision, deterministic seeds, no ground-truth use.
Validation policy: purely unsupervised on the full 10 s recording; no use of any hidden labels/true unit counts/templates. Parameters chosen conservatively for generality and speed on a single CPU thread. No duplicate events within a unit are emitted; empty output is valid if no spikes are detected.

latest_successes.description:
Lossless codec for Neuropixels int16 (little-endian) data shaped (time, channels). It uses fast, fully reversible integer transforms tailored to spatiotemporal correlations, then strong entropy coding:
- Temporal first-order differencing per channel (along rows/time).
- Spatial first-order differencing across channels (along columns).
- ZigZag mapping of signed 16-bit residuals to unsigned 16-bit magnitudes.
- Byte shuffling (all low bytes first, then all high bytes) to expose long runs of 0x00/0xFF for better compression.
- LZMA compression (preset=6) with a tiny header.
Decoding reverses: LZMA decompress → unshuffle bytes → inverse ZigZag → prefix sums across channels → prefix sums across time. All arithmetic is exact under 16-bit two’s-complement wrap-around by using 32-bit accumulators and final casting. No external metadata beyond provided shape/dtype is used. Deterministic, fast, and memory-efficient, while typically achieving strong compression on neural voltage traces.

Unsupervised, single-shot spike sorting for a 32-channel, 10 s extracellular recording. Steps:

- Template merging: build per-cluster mean templates across all 32 channels from up to 150 events/cluster (whitened). Merge clusters whose template cosine similarity > 0.95 and with primary channels within 65 µm (union-find).
- Enforce intra-unit refractory: within each unit, allow at most one spike per 12 samples, keeping the more negative amplitude event.
- Return integer array [sample_index, unit_id], sorted by sample then unit, with contiguous nonnegative unit IDs. No supervision, deterministic seeds, no ground-truth use.

Workflow: (1) For training, each 128x128 patch is featurized with pixel intensities, geometric coordinates (normalized xy), local gradients, and simple multi-scale shape-texture statistics. Only labeled regions (channel1 == 1) and valid pixels (train_y >= 0) are used. For each labeled object in a patch, we extract centroid locations and create instance-specific foreground masks. A RandomForestClassifier is trained to predict background vs punctum center. A per-training-patch global threshold is grid-searched to maximize foreground F1>0.5 under synthetic instance separation (patch-wise local IDs), using only annotated pixels. At test time, each whole test image is split into 128x128 overlapping windows (step 64). Per-pixel features are extracted and pixels are classified. Patch probabilities are averaged at overlaps. Pixelwise probability map is then thresholded and postprocessed: (a) valid extent mask applied; (b) small holes and objects <4 px are removed; (c) watershed with local maxima as seeds separates instances. Final label IDs are distinct for each test image. No pixels outside valid geometric test extent are labeled. The output is a (2,727,546) numpy array of labeled images for both test images. All computation is strictly local to individual images; no smoothing/config leakage/correlation across source fields or samples. Deterministic result due to fixed seed. No specialized packages or pretrained weights are used.
latest_successes.patch_description: Retain the original 30-tree depth-9 random forest, features, training fields, seed, one CPU thread, threshold grid and inference. Cap each tree bootstrap at 250000 draws from all eligible training pixels (instead of 16451616), chosen before test scoring after training-only profiling located the time bottleneck. This changes the fitting budget and potentially predictions; it is a manual budget adaptation, not an exact compatibility fix or an untouched GPT-4.1 score. Also pass signed int32 watershed markers as required by SciPy; confirmed by a synthetic-array compatibility probe and the preserved r3 runtime error. This avoids unsigned 8-bit label truncation.
